finalCategoryFields.summary: Basset Griffon Vendéens comprise the Grand and Petit, two French scent-hound breeds developed for hunting on foot. Their separate standards describe distinct proportions as well as different sizes.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: The Grand and Petit Basset Griffon Vendéens share a French tradition of scent hunting on foot.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Bichon names a companion-dog family that includes the Bichon Frise, Maltese, Havanese and Bolognese. The FCI groups these four together, while placing the Coton de Tuléar and Little Lion Dog in neighboring subgroups.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: The Bichon family includes the Frise, Maltese, Havanese and Bolognese, each a distinct companion breed.

finalCategoryFields.summary: The Bouvier des Flandres and Bouvier des Ardennes are distinct cattle-dog breeds. This group brings together those named Bouviers; the Flandres breed also worked as a farm draught dog.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: The Flandres and Ardennes Bouviers are distinct cattle-dog breeds with working farm histories.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Braque is a grouping of continental pointing dogs. In FCI classification it includes French braques, the Portuguese Pointer and other distinct breeds, alongside separate spaniel-type and griffon-type pointing groups.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Braque-type dogs form one FCI grouping of continental pointers, including French and Portuguese breeds.

finalCategoryFields.summary: English and American Cocker Spaniels share a history as compact sporting dogs used to hunt birds in cover. They developed into separate breeds; which one is called simply “Cocker Spaniel” depends on the country.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: English and American Cockers share sporting roots but are separate breeds with different naming traditions.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Coonhounds are scent hounds developed for following raccoons to trees. The group includes distinct breeds such as the Redbone and Bluetick; UKC hunting events test trailing and treeing work separately from conformation shows.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Coonhounds include several breeds developed for trailing raccoons and locating them in trees.

finalCategoryFields.summary: In Nordic hunting, elkhounds form a large-game working category. Norwegian kennel-club guidance includes the grey and black Norwegian Elkhounds, Jämthund and several Laikas, with different breeds used for tracking on a leash or working loose.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: In Nordic hunting, elkhounds track large game on a leash or work loose; the category spans several breeds.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Foxhounds form a family of pack-hunting scent hounds. North American working records distinguish American, English, Penn-Marydel and Crossbred lines, preserving separate breeding histories within the shared hunting tradition.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Foxhounds share a pack-hunting tradition across American, English, Penn-Marydel and Crossbred lines.

finalCategoryFields.summary: German pointers include the Shorthaired, Wirehaired, Longhaired and Roughhaired breeds, each with its own standard. These continental gundogs belong to a pointing tradition; the Shorthaired standard also describes development into a versatile hunting dog.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: German Shorthaired, Wirehaired, Longhaired and Roughhaired Pointers are distinct continental gundog breeds.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Hounds encompass diverse hunting breeds, including scent hounds that follow trails and sighthounds built for pursuit. Beagles and Whippets illustrate different branches of this group, whose hunting methods and character vary widely.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Hounds include scent-trailing and sight-pursuit breeds, from Beagles to Whippets.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Mountain-type dogs form a broad FCI grouping with varied working histories. It includes the Pyrenean Mountain Dog, a flock guardian, and the Newfoundland, whose standard describes hauling loads and working in water.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Mountain-type dogs include distinct working breeds, from Pyrenean flock guardians to Newfoundlands.

finalCategoryFields.summary: The Large and Small Münsterländer are separate German pointing breeds, not two sizes of one breed. Both belong to the longhaired pointing-dog tradition, with different documented breeding histories.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Large and Small Münsterländers are separate breeds within the German longhaired pointing tradition.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Pinschers include distinct breeds such as the German Pinscher, Miniature Pinscher and Affenpinscher. Their standards describe watch and companion roles; the name does not imply that every member shares one size, coat or character.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: German, Miniature and Affenpinschers are distinct breeds with watch and companion-dog traditions.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Retrievers were developed to find shot game and bring it back without damaging it, on land or in water. The category includes distinct breeds such as Labradors, Goldens and Curly-Coated Retrievers, with different histories and characters.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Retrievers include distinct breeds developed to recover game and carry it back gently on land or from water.

finalCategoryFields.summary: English, Gordon, Irish and Irish Red and White Setters are distinct bird-hunting breeds. They locate game and indicate its position; their name recalls the low “set” used when hunters caught birds with nets.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Four setter breeds share a bird-finding tradition, named for the low stance once used in net hunting.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Sheepdog covers breeds with different roles around flocks. Border Collies herd livestock, while the Abruzzes and Maremma Shepherd Dog chiefly protects sheep and property; both fall within the FCI sheepdog section.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Sheepdogs include flock herders and guardians, whose traditional jobs call for different working methods.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Spaniels range from sporting breeds developed to find, flush and retrieve game to toy companions. Welsh Springers illustrate the flushing branch, while Cavaliers and English Toy Spaniels belong to companion branches.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Spaniels span working bird dogs and toy companions, with distinct breeds and different traditional roles.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Spitz is a broad dog type, often marked by upright ears and a dense coat. Its members have varied histories: Malamutes hauled heavy sled loads, Finnish Spitz located game birds, and Samoyeds worked with northern herders.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: Spitz-type breeds have varied hunting, herding and sled-working histories; they are not one breed.

finalCategoryFields.summary: English and Welsh Springer Spaniels are separate flushing-dog breeds. Both belong to the bird-hunting spaniel tradition; the English breed’s history includes springing game for nets, falcons and later guns.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: English and Welsh Springers are separate spaniel breeds with a shared game-flushing tradition.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Swiss mountain dogs, or Sennenhunde, comprise the Bernese, Greater Swiss, Appenzeller and Entlebucher breeds. Their Swiss farm histories include cattle work, guarding and, especially in the larger breeds, pulling carts.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: The four Sennenhunde breeds share Swiss farm roots, with cattle, guarding and draught-working traditions.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Terriers developed around vermin hunting and related farm or household work. The group ranges from small Cairn and Border Terriers to the much larger Airedale; its members have distinct breed histories and builds.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: A vermin-hunting breed group ranging from small Cairn and Border Terriers to the much larger Airedale.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Water Dog is a group name used by the FCI for breeds including the Barbet, Portuguese Water Dog and Lagotto Romagnolo. Their work differs: the Lagotto’s registry history traces a change from marsh retrieving to searching for truffles.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: An FCI category including Barbet, Portuguese Water Dog and Lagotto Romagnolo, whose work now includes truffle hunting.

finalCategoryFields.summary: Water spaniels include the distinct Irish and American Water Spaniel breeds. The Irish standard describes hunting and retrieving in heavy cover and a traditional wildfowling role; the American was developed to retrieve from small boats as well as work on land.
finalCategoryFields.shortDescription: A water-working spaniel category including the distinct Irish and American Water Spaniel breeds.
